title: Bubble Sort and Insertion Sort
intro: A short, self-paced catch-up covering the essential lesson ideas. Check every question, then correct anything missed.

stages.label: Remember
stages.lead: Retrieve two ideas from earlier learning.

questions.prompt: Does linear search require a sorted list?
questions.feedback: A linear search simply scans items in sequence.

questions.prompt: What happens when the CPU executes an instruction?
options: The specified operation is carried out
The keyboard must always be read
questions.answer: The specified operation is carried out
questions.feedback: The execute stage carries out the decoded operation.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the key concepts, visual model and worked explanation.

blocks.title: Bubble sort
blocks.text: Compare adjacent values and swap those in the wrong order; repeat passes until no swaps are needed.

blocks.title: After each pass
blocks.text: For ascending bubble sort, the largest remaining value moves towards the end on each full pass.

blocks.title: Insertion sort
blocks.text: Treat the first item as a sorted section; take the next key item and insert it into the correct place.

blocks.title: Keep a trace
blocks.text: Show each swap or insertion rather than jumping straight to the final sorted result.

blocks.title: Visual model · Bubble Sort and Insertion Sort
blocks.caption: Insertion sort is different: it inserts each next key into the correctly positioned place of the growing sorted section.

blocks.title: Worked example · Show one full bubble-sort pass through [5, 1, 4, 2].
blocks.text: Compare 5 and 1: swap → [1, 5, 4, 2]. Compare 5 and 4: swap → [1, 4, 5, 2]. Compare 5 and 2: swap → [1, 4, 2, 5]. End of first pass: 5 has reached its final position. More passes are needed to sort the remaining values.

items: bubble sort — Repeatedly compares and swaps adjacent out-of-order values.
insertion sort — Inserts each next item into a growing sorted section.
pass — One traversal of adjacent values in a sort.
key — Current value being inserted into a sorted section.

options: Only the first and last values

questions.prompt: What does insertion sort build as it runs?
questions.feedback: It inserts the next item into an already sorted section.

questions.prompt: For ascending bubble sort, what generally moves to the end after a full pass?
questions.feedback: Adjacent swaps push a large value toward the end of the unsorted portion.

stages.label: Practise
stages.lead: Match and reorder before applying the method yourself.

blocks.text: Trace each adjacent swap in order, then check the evolving sorted portion.

questions.prompt: Match each sorting term to its description.
pairs: Insert a key into sorted part
questions.feedback: Bubble sorts by passes; insertion grows its sorted section.

questions.prompt: Order the changes in one bubble-sort pass of [5,1,4,2].
questions.feedback: Swap 5 with 1, then 4, then 2, moving 5 to the end.

questions.prompt: One bubble-sort pass on [4,2,3] needs how many swaps to reach [2,3,4]?
Insertion sort has [2,6] sorted and must insert 5. Where does it go?
questions.feedback: Insertion puts the key in its ordered position.

stages.label: Apply
stages.lead: Predict the Code First result and write one exam-style answer.

blocks.title: Code First · Predict → Write → Test → Improve
blocks.caption: Predict the printed file size. Change a to 1. Explain how comparing file sizes helps calculate total storage requirements.

blocks.text: Explain how insertion sort orders the list [4, 1, 3]. [4 marks]

questions.prompt: The code starts a = 4, b = 2, swaps when a > b and prints a. What is printed?
If a starts at 1 and b stays 2, what does it print?
questions.feedback: No swap is needed because 1 is less than 2.

questions.prompt: What is the insertion-sort result of [4,1,3]?

writing.prompt: Explain how insertion sort orders the list [4, 1, 3]. [4 marks]
writing.model: First item 4 is initial sorted section [1]; insert 1 before 4 → [1, 4, 3] [1]; take key 3 [1]; insert between 1 and 4 → [1, 3, 4] [1].
checklist: I explained the initial sorted section.
I traced inserting the next key correctly.
I gave the final ordered list.

stages.label: Check
stages.lead: Check your understanding and review your mastery result.

questions.prompt: Bubble sort may require several passes to sort a list.
questions.feedback: One pass moves one large value into place, but others may remain unordered.

questions.prompt: Insertion sort compares only adjacent pairs and repeats full bubble passes.
questions.feedback: Insertion takes the next key and places it into the sorted section.

questions.prompt: A temporary variable can prevent losing a value when swapping two variables.
questions.feedback: The temporary value holds one original value while the other is overwritten.
